content: What are the four core functions of the NIST AI RMF?

The NIST AI Risk Management Framework’s Core is organized around four high‑level functions:

**GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, and MANAGE**【Source 1, Page 25】【Source 2, Page 8】
Governance is the cross‑cutting function; it is intended to inform and be infused throughout the other three functions (MAP, MEASURE, and MANAGE)【Source 2, Page 25】.
What is the purpose of the NIST AI RMF?

The NIST AI Risk Management Framework is intended to give organizations a structured way to manage the risks of AI systems and to ensure those systems are trustworthy—​valid, reliable, safe, secure, resilient, accountable, transparent, explainable, privacy‑enhanced, and fair.  Its “Core” defines four functions (GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, MANAGE) that can be applied throughout the AI lifecycle to address risk in practice【Document 5, Page 8】.

The AI Risk Management Framework is intended for **organizations** that develop, deploy, or use AI systems and need to manage the associated risks — it provides a set of functions (GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, MANAGE) to help organizations address AI‑related risks throughout the AI lifecycle【Source 5, Page 8】.
